data.title: Kinetic Energy Explorer
data.description: Examine how mass and velocity non-linearly dictate kinetic energy, highlighting the quadratic sensitivity of velocity versus the linear proportionality of mass.
data.context: Classical mechanics in physics, modeling the energy possessed by an object due to its motion, crucial for analyzing collisions, work, and conservation principles.

parameters.name: Mass
parameters.description: The inertial mass of the moving body

parameters.name: Velocity
parameters.description: The instantaneous linear velocity of the body

observations.trigger: Isolate the mass variable by keeping velocity constant at 5.0 m/s and incrementally double the mass from 4.0 kg to 8.0 kg, then to 16.0 kg.
observations.prompt: Observe how the resulting kinetic energy scales proportionally with mass. Deduce why the kinetic energy-to-mass ratio remains invariant despite changes in the scalar mass value.

observations.trigger: Lock the mass parameter at a baseline of 4.0 kg while systematically increasing velocity from 5.0 m/s to 10.0 m/s.
observations.prompt: Examine the non-linear trajectory of the kinetic energy output as velocity doubles. Formulate an explanation regarding the exponential magnitude shift rooted in the velocity squared term within classical mechanics.

challenges.instruction: Examine the kinetic energy formula KE = 0.5 * m * v^2. Determine which parameter exerts a disproportionately greater influence on the resulting kinetic energy when independently doubled from its default baseline.
